newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Issue date May 16 for T$6.8 bln Taiwan-dollar bond.
newsitem.headline: Issue date May 16 for T$6.8 bln Taiwan-dollar bond.

text.p: The Central American Bank of Economic Integration has set a May 16 issue date for its planned T$6.8 billion (US$246 million) Taiwan dollar-denominated bond issue, lead underwriter Citibank of Taiwan said on Friday.
The issue would have a five-year term and a coupon rate of 7.35 percent, with interests paid semi-annually and principal payment at the end of year five, Citibank said in a statement.
The bond would be issued at par, Citibank said.
Citibank first confirmed the issue on Tuesday and said other underwriters included International Commercial Bank of China and Bank of Taiwan.
The Central Bank of Economic Integration, based in Honduras, would become the second development bank to issue Taiwan dollar bonds.
The Asian Development Bank issued T$2.6 billion (US$100 million) worth of Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds in August 1995, and launched a T$7 billion (US$255 million) issue in December 1996.
Analysts have said the issues reflected a drive by Taiwan's government to encourage international agencies to raise capital in the island's cash-flush money market.
